tasks.title: Network board: a container network by hand, NAT
tasks.statement: Repeat what Docker does for a container: a namespace, a veth pair, a bridge with the gateway address, a default route in the container, packet forwarding in the host and a masquerade rule. The board traces a ping step by step and shows where it breaks. Five scenarios: build the network from scratch, find the missing masquerade rule, find forwarding that is switched off (ip_forward), find the missing default route and publish a container port with a DNAT rule. The exercise is solved when all scenarios are solved.
tasks.hint: A packet for another network goes to the gateway; the gateway has to forward packets and have a leg in the destination network. The outside network does not know private addresses: without masquerade the reply does not come back. A port can be published only with a DNAT rule that points at a host inside.
